answer.answer: Prioritize the `/in/playerActivity` cache-miss path: keep stale data available while one background worker refreshes it, preventing web requests from running the Redis shard scan and aggregation. Separately, make `/p/:identifier/raids` render shell plus local raid statistics first; defer collectibles enrichment and load Pantheon only when its tab is selected, or share/cache its collectibles fetch.

claims.value: The highest-value non-profile target is the `/in/playerActivity` cache-miss path. It serves a heavily used analytics surface: RUM recorded 13,210 calls over 7 days with avg 3.69 s, p75 1.09 s, and p95 12.03 s; APM recorded 23,255 exact `GET /in/playerActivity` spans with avg 1.99 s, p75 2 ms, and p95 13.03 s. The 2 ms APM p75 alongside the 13.03 s p95 indicates a fast cached path and a severe slow tail. Logs from the last 24h recorded 68 foreground rebuilds and 204 shard logs, with shard-scan p95 about 18 s and math p95 about 16 s. This has greater demonstrated reach than `/in/meta` (4,641 spans over 7 days) and the very slow leaderboard CSV export (only 28 calls in 24h).

Proposed intervention: implement stale-while-revalidate for `apiPlayerActivity`, using a longer stale TTL and a single-flight/background refresh lock. `apiPlayerActivity` currently reads the `apiPlayerActivity` cache and falls back synchronously to `memcache.GetPlayerActivity`; meanwhile `sweeperbot.cachePlayerActivity` writes every 5 minutes with a 5 minute TTL. That equal refresh/expiry cadence creates a window where a web request can miss and pay the Redis scan and aggregation. Keep the last successful value serveable, let only the background refresher rebuild it, preserve stale data if refresh fails, and follow the existing Discord behavior of not rebuilding in the request/command path when cache data is absent.

answer.answer: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer—not a retrieval product or notes system. It must preserve learned knowledge together with resumable work state and evidence. claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer for agents. It is an agent-first durable machine-continuity product and protocol, not primarily a notes app, wiki, synchronized folder, transcript archive, retrieval system/product, or memory database. Its purpose is to let agents learn, continue, and iteratively advance complex work across research, planning, implementation, operations, verification, and handoff.

Beyond learned or semantic memory, Straylight must durably preserve the live state needed to resume and advance work: goals, evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved/open questions, rejected paths or approaches, checkpoints, current state, and resumable next actions. The workspace must be reopenable, queryable, computable, revisable, verifiable, checkpointable, and handoff-ready; task-scoped checkpoints are refreshed independently from semantic-memory promotion. Full source artifacts and evidence remain available, with immutable source episodes, corrections, versions, provenance, authority, valid time, and transaction time; summaries, embeddings, indexes, context packs, and consolidated memory are derived, reversible aids rather than truth boundaries.

Obsidian is not the product boundary because Straylight's canonical interaction model is agent-first durable machine continuity, not human note filing or raw Markdown storage. Obsidian and Markdown are useful prototype inputs/corpora, human-readable projections, evaluation material, and export formats, but they are neither the canonical product boundary nor necessarily the canonical storage representation. Metis organizes the human knowledge base and supplies the first representative corpus; Straylight is the separate portable agent context and durable-work product designed over that kind of corpus.

The first benchmark was too narrow because it evaluated retrieval readiness rather than the full durable-work product: its corpus had 44 non-private notes from Metis, N24 RaceWatch, Home Network Improvements, and Straylight, with 20 frozen questions and 53 gold evidence items, and the prototype exercised `memory.open`, `memory.query`, and `memory.read` but not model-directed `memory.compute` or `memory.verify`. Policy 0.2 reached 17 of 20 cases and 46 of 53 evidence items at 11,999 characters P95 context, while one-shot top-k also reached 17 of 20 cases, recovered 48 of 53 evidence items, and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932 for the workspace; therefore the workspace did not beat one-shot top-k on aggregate recall or cost and has not cleared its justification gate. Policy 0.2 is frozen only as a regression baseline, and its tuned result is not holdout evidence. The expanded primary evaluation must use untouched, blinded cases and compare direct filesystem search/range reads/scripts, an agent-first workspace with model-directed `open`, `query`, `read`, `compute`, `verify`, checkpoint, and revision behavior, and fixed handoff/context packs. It must prove that a fresh agent can resume, iterate after changed constraints, compute, verify before action, inspect full sources, reason about time, supersession and contradictions, continue incidents and operational learning, and leave correct durable next-state and handoff artifacts. Required real workloads are Warmind/Charlemagne performance and incident work, StarRupture factory planning, Switzerland trip planning—including booked-versus-proposed state—and Straylight's own evolution. No canonical storage-engine decision is justified until that blinded model-answer evaluation tests model-directed workspace calls against an untouched holdout set.
